lawyer:
Sagir Hossain, Advocate ----- For the Petitioners. 
Sikder Mahmudur Razi, Advocate ----- For the Respondent No. 7.
parties:
Atigullah (Md) and others  ----- Petitioners
Vs.
Artha Rin Adalat and others ----- Respondent
full_judgment:
Md Anwarul Haque J: On an application, at the instance of one Haji Md. Atiq Ullah son of late Ahsan Ullah, Chairman & Managing Director, Millat Corporation Pvt. Ltd, Md. Rabi Ullah son of Haji Md. Atiq Ullah, Director of Millat Corporation Pvt. Ltd, Mosammat Bashir-un-nessa wife of Haji Md. Atiq Ullah, Director of Millat Corporation Pvt. Ltd, Md. Hafiz son of Haji Md. Atiq Ullah, Director of Millat Corporation Pvt. Ltd, Abdul Majid son of Haji Md. Atiq Ullah Director of Millat Corporation Pvt. Ltd, Md. Jafar Ullah son of Haji Md. Atiq Ullah, Director of Millat Corporation Pvt. Ltd, Md. Rafique, son of Haji Md. Atiq Ullah, Director of Millat Corporation Pvt.. Ltd, Md. Aminullah Khokan son of Haji Md. Atiq Ullah, Director of Millat Corporation Pvt. Ltd, under Article 102 of the Constitution of the People's Republic of Bangladesh this rule was issued calling upon the respondents to show cause as to why the impugned provision laid down in Section 33(7) of the Artha Rin Adalat Ain, 2003 (Act VIII of 2003) (Annexure-A to the petition) shall not be declared unconstitutional and void as being violative of Articles 26, 31 and 42 of the Constitution and also issuance of the certificates by the Artha Rin Adalat under Section 33(7) of the Artha Rin Adalat Ain, 2003 in execution Case No. 221 of 2007 in favour of the decree-holder, Annexure-J to the petition, shall not be declared to have been made without lawful authority and is of no legal effect and/or such other or further order or orders passed as to this Court may seem fit and proper. 

 4. It is the case of the petitioners that ultimately such suit has been decreed on contest on 30-5-2007 for recovery of amount from the petitioner-judgment-debtor to the tune to Taka 74,33,448 with interest under the provision laid down in section 50(2) of the Artha Rin Adalat Ain, 2003 affording an opportunity judgment debtor to pay such amount within 60(sixty) days from the date; in default decree-holder will be at liberty to realize the amount in accordance with law. However, petitioners have not yet paid the decreetal amount where decree holder filed Execution Case No. 221 of 2007 on 28-5-2008 for the realization to the tune of Taka 82,55,406 as on 31-10-2007. Thereafter observing all the formalities required by law the learned Judge of the Artha Rin Adalat issued a certificate under Section 33(7) of the Artha Rin. Adalat Ain, 2003 on 11-6-2009 and disposed of the Execution Case under the provision laid down in section 33(9) of the Artha Rin Adalat Ain, 2003. Now the judgment-debtor the present petitioners have jumped upon the High Court Division to . invoke the writ jurisdiction challenging vires of the provisions of Section 33(7) of the Artha Rin Adalat Ain, 2003 which is allegedly found inconsistent with the provision laid down in article 26, 31 and 42 of the Constitution of People's Republic of Bangladesh. 

 5. Mr. Md. Sagir Hossain the learned Advocate appearing on behalf of the petitioners have tried to argue that the provision laid down in section 33(7) is inconsistent with the provision of Article 32 and 42 of the Constitution and accordingly this provisions is to be knocked down under Article 26 of the Constitution of Bangladesh. Moreover the issuance of the Certificate by the Artha Rin Adalat transferring the title of the mortgagor-judgment-debtor in favour of the decree holder over the schedule property, valued five times of the decreetal amount, is absolutely illegal because decree holder is not entitled to realize more than decreetal amount from the judgment-debtor, the petitioner. Moreover the learned Advocate appearing on behalf of the petitioner has claimed that he has already paid the decreetal amount; as such, issuance of such certificate under section 33(7) has become redundant one which will go to make the judgment debtor homeless. 

 7. The learned Advocate has drawn our attention in the above Article of the Constitution where it dealt with acquisition of the property only in accordance with law but in the instant case the property was given in mortgage in accordance with law but in the instant case the property was given in mortgage in accordance with law executing a Power of Attorney to sell or transfer the property for the purpose of realization of the outstanding loan from the loanee. Even the issuance of certificate under section 33(7) is supported by law. In such circumstance we find no manner of application of the provisions of Article 32 and 42 of the Constitution of the People's Republic of Bangladesh. In fact, the very process of auction is the product of law which cannot be said inconsistent with the provisions of Article 32 and 42 of the Constitution. In support of his contention the learned Advocate appearing on behalf of the respondent has referred a decision of a case Setara vs Al-Amin reported in 61 DLR 791 where their lordships have observed that provisions of section 33(5) and 33(7) of the Artha Rin Adalat Ain, 2003 have been incorporated in the Act VIII of 2003 in order to transfer the title of the Judgment debtor to the decree holder when process of realization the decreetal amount will fail by auction sale. So, in no circumstance this piece of legislation can be declared inconsistent with the provisions of Article 32 and 42 of the Constitution. Moreover, the learned Advocate appearing on behalf of the respondent has also argued that in no occasion judgment debtor has paid any amount in order to re-pay the decreetal amount in question. He goes to argues that depositing some money in a current account belonging to the petitioners does not speak or bear any evidence of payment of the decreetal amount passed in the Artha Rin Adalat Ain Suit No.51 of 2006, in Artha Rin Adalat No.2. 

 8. In fine, the learned Advocate has argued that in a writ petition No.1165 of 2009 this judgment debtor-petitioners have been asked to pay 50% of the decreetal amount within 10 days but unfortunately without availing such an opportunity this judgment debtor-petitioners allowed the Court to discharge the Rule and thereafter again he has come with a identical prayer which should not be allowed to continue. 

 9. On the face of the submission we have gone through the provision laid down in Article 42 and 31 of the Constitution but we find no scope to say that the provision laid in Section 33(7) in any way is found to be inconsistent the provision laid down in the Constitution and hence we find no merit in the Rule in that Court. Moreover, the judgment-debtor has paid no decreetal amount till now through they have so asserted at the time of hearing this application. In Supplementary affidavit he has simply annexed a deposit slip dated 44-2010 where pay order No. 0018601/ 39/101 is found to have been deposited in the current account of Millat Corporation Pvt. Ltd. belonging to the petitioners which does not bear any evidence of payment of the decreetal amount to the extent of Taka 46,00,000 out of Taka 82,55,406 rather it is a step to deceive the decree holder which must be condemned.
